title: Parallel DAG Workflow Engine
summary: C++20 workflow engine for dependency-aware parallel scheduling, bounded execution, cancellation, and failure propagation.
importance: Reliable workflow infrastructure must preserve dependency and shutdown invariants while extracting useful parallelism from complex task graphs.
highlights: Executed dependency graphs with a fixed worker pool, bounded queues, and deterministic failure propagation, validated against a single-threaded reference executor.
Measured ~1.6x throughput on wide graphs (3.28 ms to 2.06 ms) and ~1.66x on layered graphs at 4 workers, with chains correctly showing no speedup.
Validated cancellation and race-safe shutdown with ThreadSanitizer and a 67-test suite.
imageAlt: Bar charts comparing single-threaded reference and multi-worker execution time for a 32-task wide graph and a 4x4 layered graph.

title: Distributed Model Server
summary: Local-first distributed inference service that routes and batches ONNX requests across gRPC workers.
importance: Model quality is not enough in production; inference systems also need bounded work, health checks, failure recovery, and reproducible performance.
highlights: Built a FastAPI gateway and gRPC/Protobuf worker service for ONNX inference.
Implemented request batching, bounded queues, health checks, retries, and graceful shutdown.
Recorded a local benchmark of 366.43 successful requests/sec with 45.56 ms p99 latency across 3,663 requests.
imageAlt: Bar chart of p50, p95, and p99 end-to-end latency and a histogram of request durations from a 3,663-request local benchmark.

title: High-Performance Event Streaming Engine
summary: Linux C++20 event-streaming engine using deterministic partitioning, nonblocking UDP, bounded queues, and multithreaded aggregation.
importance: Streaming systems need predictable behavior under load, including backpressure, overload handling, deterministic routing, and clean shutdown.
highlights: Built a deterministic routing and aggregation engine over nonblocking UDP with epoll, bounded per-worker queues, and multithreaded aggregation.
Processed ~1.1M events/sec at 0% loss with batch framing, and sustained a paced 200K events/sec with sub-millisecond p99 end-to-end latency in the committed local benchmark.
Validated overload handling, duplicate/reorder rejection, and graceful shutdown with 135 tests passing under ASan/UBSan and ThreadSanitizer.
imageAlt: Bar chart of median throughput across batch sizes and a paced 200K events-per-second sustained load with sub-millisecond p99 latency.

title: Infrared Object Detection Pipeline
summary: Infrared person-detection system designed to support drone-based search-and-rescue workflows.
importance: It applies computer vision to a concrete safety problem and shows the full ML loop from annotation conversion through training, evaluation, and inference.
highlights: Fine-tuned YOLOv8n with PyTorch/CUDA on 5,548 infrared images, reaching 85.9% mAP50 on validation data.
Built a COCO-to-YOLO conversion pipeline for 6,546 person bounding boxes.
Implemented GPU training, evaluation, checkpointing, and batch inference, measuring 3.1 ms per image.
imageAlt: Infrared night-vision image showing detected people outlined with bounding boxes from the YOLOv8 validation set.

title: Order Book Simulator
summary: Deterministic C++20 replay engine that reconstructs Level 2 order books, validates market-event integrity, and simulates fee-aware IOC execution.
importance: Market-data systems must preserve ordering, reject malformed state, and model execution precisely before their outputs can support trustworthy analysis.
highlights: Reconstructed order-book state while detecting stale, duplicate, out-of-order, and malformed market events.
Implemented fee-aware IOC execution with fixed-point arithmetic and depth modeling.
Processed 100,000 accepted events at 12,508.74 events/sec in the committed deterministic benchmark.
imageAlt: Bar chart showing deterministic replay throughput and event integrity counts (accepted, duplicates, gaps, malformed, book errors) from a 100,000-event replay.

title: Finance Data Pipeline
summary: Serverless AWS pipeline that ingests stock-market data, transforms it into partitioned Parquet, and exposes it through Glue and Athena.
importance: Analytics systems become cheaper and easier to operate when ingestion, schema conversion, partitioning, catalog registration, and scheduling are automated as one reproducible pipeline.
highlights: Built Python Lambda functions for scheduled ingestion and event-driven transformation of Alpha Vantage market data.
Wrote typed Parquet datasets partitioned by symbol, year, and month and registered them in AWS Glue for Athena queries.
Defined Lambda, S3, Glue, Athena, IAM, and EventBridge infrastructure with Terraform.
imageAlt: Architecture diagram showing EventBridge, ingest Lambda, raw S3, transform Lambda, curated Parquet with Glue catalog, and Athena.
